issues.legal_issue: Uncultivated banjar land that is not occupied or let for agricultural purposes is excluded when calculating whether a landowner is a small landowner and whether the holding is surplus.
material_facts: The landowners’ holdings were assessed as of the date the Act came into force.
After uncultivated banjar land was excluded, each landowner’s holding was below the permissible area.
The tenants sought to purchase surplus land, but the authorities found no surplus area.
issues.conclusion: Uncultivated banjar land could not be included in calculating the landowners’ holdings, and the tenants’ purchase applications were rightly dismissed because no surplus area remained.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(2) and 2(8) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, read with section 4(1) of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887, land for this purpose must be occupied or let for agricultural or related purposes. Banjar Kadim and Banjar Jadid do not fall within that definition. The relevant holdings are assessed as of the commencement of the 1953 Act. The Court relied on Bhagwan Das v. State of Punjab and Munshi Ram v. Financial Commissioner, Haryana.

predicates.tenant_surplus_purchase_proceeding: A tenant sought to purchase land alleged to be surplus to a landowner’s permissible holding.
predicates.holding_assessed_at_commencement: The landowner’s holding was assessed as it stood when the relevant land-ceiling scheme began.
predicates.uncultivated_banjar_not_used_for_agricul: The land in question was uncultivated banjar land and was not occupied or let for agricultural or related purposes.

issues.definition: When a tenant’s purchase claim depends on whether a holding is surplus, uncultivated banjar land not used for agriculture is left out of the holding assessed at commencement.

issues.legal_issue: A landowner whose holding does not exceed the permissible area is not required to make a reservation of land.
material_facts: The landowners had made no reservation under the relevant provisions.
Their holdings, calculated after excluding banjar land, were below the permissible area.
The dispute arose in proceedings concerning tenant purchases and the landowners’ claim to small-landowner status.
issues.conclusion: A small landowner was not obliged to make a reservation, and failure to do so did not attract the consequences prescribed for non-reservation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3, 4, 5, 5A and 5B of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, make reservation relevant where a landowner holds land in excess of the permissible area. The Act’s ceiling scheme makes excess land available as surplus, while reservation gives an over-limit landowner an option to select land to retain. The Court also relied on sections 5C, 9(1)(i) and 18, and on Gurbux Singh v. State of Punjab and Bhagwan Das v. State of Punjab.

predicates.landowner_status_dispute: The dispute concerned whether a landowner was a small landowner and whether the landowner had to reserve land.
predicates.holding_not_above_permissible_area: The landowner’s holding did not exceed the permissible area.
predicates.no_reservation_made: The landowner had not selected and reserved land for retention.

issues.definition: If the dispute concerns reservation and the landowner’s holding does not exceed the permissible area, the absence of a reservation does not create a duty to make one.

issues.legal_issue: A new contention dependent on facts not raised earlier and absent from the record will not be entertained for the first time on appeal.
material_facts: The tenants argued for the first time before the Supreme Court that a particular area had been wrongly excluded because it was occupied by old tenants.
The point had not been raised at any earlier stage.
The record contained no facts about that area.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to permit the tenants to raise the contention for the first time on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the contention as a factual issue that had not been raised below and for which the record contained no supporting facts, and therefore declined to consider it for the first time on appeal.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: A party presented a contention to an appellate court.
predicates.contention_not_raised_below: The party had not raised that contention before the lower decision-makers.
predicates.necessary_facts_absent_from_record: The record did not contain facts needed to decide the contention.

issues.definition: In an appeal, a contention first raised there is not entertained when its necessary factual basis is absent from the record.
